questions.question: What does Dapper do, and who calls it?
questions.answer: Dapper is a .NET micro-ORM library consumed by application code using ADO.NET connections. Connection extension methods execute SQL and return mapped rows or affected-row counts, with synchronous/asynchronous and buffered/unbuffered options. Equivalent terminology for the named source definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.
requiredFacts: Dapper is a .NET micro-ORM library consumed by application code using ADO.NET connections.

questions.question: Name the principal components and their responsibilities.
questions.answer: Dapper is the core library. Dapper.EntityFramework provides EntityFramework extension handlers. Dapper.Rainbow supplies CRUD helpers on Dapper; Dapper.SqlBuilder composes SQL queries dynamically. Equivalent terminology for the named source definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.

Dapper.EntityFramework provides EntityFramework extension handlers.

questions.answer: The implementation is C#, including SqlMapper and CommandDefinition. SDK-style .NET projects define package boundaries; Dapper targets net461, netstandard2.0, net8.0 and net10.0. Dapper.SqlBuilder is a distinct SDK project referencing Dapper. Equivalent terminology for the named source definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.

questions.answer: SqlMapper.Execute(this IDbConnection cnn, string sql, ...) is the extension entry. It constructs CommandDefinition with the supplied SQL and parameters and forwards to ExecuteImpl. questions.question: Where is X, synchronous single-command non-query execution, implemented?
questions.answer: Dapper/SqlMapper.cs defines ExecuteCommand. It obtains a command through CommandDefinition.SetupCommand, opens a previously closed connection, calls ExecuteNonQuery, calls OnCompleted and returns the affected-row result. Finally it restores a previously closed connection to closed and clears/disposes the command. Equivalent terminology for the named source definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.

questions.question: For R, connection.Execute(sql) with null parameters, give the source-supported path to the affected-row result and its unresolved boundaries.
questions.answer: SqlMapper.Execute creates CommandDefinition then calls ExecuteImpl. With null parameters the non-multi-execution branch reaches ExecuteCommand with a null parameter reader. ExecuteCommand calls SetupCommand and then IDbCommand.ExecuteNonQuery, returns its result and performs cleanup. SetupCommand calls IDbConnection.CreateCommand; actual database/provider behavior behind the interfaces is external dynamic dispatch and is not established by these sources. Equivalent terminology for the named source definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.

Example usage:

```csharp
var count = connection.Execute(@"
  set nocount on
  create table #t(i int)
  set nocount off
  insert #t
  select @a a union all select @b
  set nocount on
  drop table #t", new {a=1, b=2 });
Assert.Equal(2, count);
```

questions.question: Where does Z, the SQL string supplied to Execute, enter and get handled?
questions.answer: Execute passes sql into the CommandDefinition constructor. The constructor stores it as CommandText and infers CommandType when none is provided. SetupCommand assigns CommandText to the provider command before execution; this assignment is not an SQL parser or an injection-safety guarantee. Equivalent terminology for the named source definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.
